description: Iron-rich protein in red blood cells carrying oxygen from the lungs to tissues.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Low levels may indicate iron deficiency anemia or chronic blood loss. Maintain iron-rich foods (spinach, legumes, lean meat) and Vitamin C.

description: Count of oxygen-carrying red cells in circulation.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Hydration and adequate B12/folate support healthy red cell turnover.

description: Immune defense cells fighting infection, inflammation, and cellular stress.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Elevated counts often reflect recent immune response or acute stress. Adequate rest and immune support are recommended.

description: Cell fragments essential for normal blood clotting and vessel repair.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Crucial for hemostasis; report any unexpected bruising or mucosal bleeding to your physician.

description: Proportion of total blood volume made up of red blood cells.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Elevated in dehydration or high altitudes; lower in anemia.

description: Circulating blood sugar concentration after an 8-12 hour fast.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Values 100-125 mg/dL reflect impaired fasting glucose. Emphasize low glycemic index whole foods, fiber, and regular physical activity.

description: Three-month rolling average of blood glucose saturation on hemoglobin molecules.
dietary_lifestyle_context: 5.7-6.4% indicates prediabetes range. Regular aerobic exercise and carbohydrate moderation assist healthy glucose management.

description: Total measure of all cholesterol fractions circulating in serum.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Desirable level is below 200 mg/dL. Mediterranean diet rich in monounsaturated fats and soluble fiber supports healthy lipid levels.

description: High-density lipoprotein scavenging excess cholesterol and delivering it to the liver.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Higher is protective (>50 mg/dL). Boosted by brisk walking, omega-3 fatty acids, and smoking cessation.

description: Low-density lipoprotein that can contribute to arterial plaque accumulation.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Optimal is <100 mg/dL. Reduce saturated and trans fats; increase plant sterols and soluble fiber.

description: Common type of fat in the bloodstream derived from excess dietary energy intake.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Elevated triglycerides respond well to reducing refined sugars, alcohol, and simple carbs.

description: Waste byproduct of muscle metabolism filtered almost entirely by healthy kidneys.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Ensure adequate daily water hydration. Avoid unnecessary NSAID overuse.

description: Amount of nitrogen in the blood derived from urea waste produced in the liver.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Elevated in dehydration, high protein intake, or reduced renal clearance.

description: Estimated glomerular filtration rate calculating overall renal filtering efficiency.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Values >= 90 are optimal. Values 60-89 indicate mild reduction. Maintain blood pressure within normal limits.

description: End-product of purine metabolism.
dietary_lifestyle_context: High levels can form crystals in joints (gout). Limit red meat, shellfish, and high fructose corn syrup.

description: Enzyme concentrated primarily inside liver cells, released upon hepatocellular irritation.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Elevations suggest liver stress. Minimize alcohol, avoid unnecessary hepatotoxic medications, and maintain a balanced diet.

description: Enzyme present in liver, heart, and muscle tissue.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Interpreted alongside ALT to assess hepatic and muscular health.

description: Enzyme related to the bile ducts in the liver and bone metabolism.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Elevated in biliary obstruction, bone growth/repair, or vitamin D deficiency.

description: Yellow pigment produced during the normal breakdown of red blood cells.
dietary_lifestyle_context: High levels may cause jaundice. Consult doctor for detailed fractionation (Direct vs Indirect).

description: Pituitary hormone regulating the production of thyroid hormones T3 and T4.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Elevated TSH signals underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism); low TSH suggests hyperthyroidism. Ensure adequate dietary iodine.

description: Active circulating unbound thyroxine hormone.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Works in tandem with TSH to monitor metabolic energy rate.

description: Primary circulating reservoir of Vitamin D essential for bone health and immunity.
dietary_lifestyle_context: <20 ng/mL is deficient. Moderate sunlight exposure and fortified dairy/mushrooms support synthesis.

description: Essential water-soluble vitamin required for neurological function and RBC production.
dietary_lifestyle_context: Strict vegetarians/vegans benefit from fortified nutritional yeast or doctor-approved supplementation.

description: Systemic inflammatory biomarker produced by the liver.
dietary_lifestyle_context: <1.0 mg/L indicates low cardiovascular inflammatory risk. Anti-inflammatory lifestyle (exercise, omega-3, sleep) helps lower levels.
